title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Discover the functional student spaces and quiet corners of Dickinson College that go beyond the standard admissions route, from specialized reading rooms to newly renovated hubs.

cards.title: Upper Level Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Quiet enclosed spaces with tech integration
cards.notes: Reserve one of 13 enclosed rooms for group work; upper-level spots include flat panel monitors and USB-C connectivity for collaborative projects.
cards.short_summary: Enclosed group study rooms in the main library equipped with collaborative technology.
cards.evidence_claim: The library has 13 study rooms located on the upper, main, and lower levels, with upper and main level rooms featuring flat panel monitors and USB-C capability.
cards.source_title: Study Room Use & Reservation Guidelines - Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Reservations must be made 8 hours in advance; sessions last up to three hours per day.

cards.title: Tome Science Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Second floor specialized library
cards.notes: Visit the second floor for a quiet atmosphere surrounded by physics and math journals; it offers large windows with views of the academic quad.
cards.short_summary: A specialized reading room on the second floor of Tome Hall focused on science and mathematics.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tome Science Reading Room is located on the second floor of Tome and is open to students, staff, and faculty at all times for consulting specialized journals.
cards.source_title: Tome Science Reading Room | Dickinson College
cards.access_notes: Open to students, staff, and faculty at all times.

cards.title: Rector Interaction Spaces
cards.subtitle: Collaborative nooks in the science wing
cards.notes: Utilize the modern 'interaction spaces' designed for interdisciplinary work; these comfortable seating areas are popular for impromptu study sessions.
cards.short_summary: Modern collaborative work and study spaces integrated throughout the Rector Science Complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rector Science Complex includes comfortable collaborative work and study spaces designed to bring students and professors together across disciplines.
cards.source_title: A Look Inside Dickinson College's Rector Science Complex
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; primarily used by science students but open to all.

cards.title: The HUB Underground
cards.subtitle: Lower level social and study lounge
cards.notes: Check out the new 'bed-like' seating arrangements tucked under the stairs for a relaxed, homey environment during long breaks between classes.
cards.short_summary: A newly renovated lower-level lounge area in the student union featuring unique furniture.
cards.evidence_claim: The HUB renovation introduced new student gathering areas, including large seating arrangements tucked under the stairs in the HUB Underground.
cards.source_title: Students concerned over glimpses of HUB renovations - The Dickinsonian
cards.access_notes: Open during HUB operating hours; late night access typically available during the semester.

cards.title: Althouse Hall Lounge
cards.subtitle: Quiet academic quad retreat
cards.notes: Find the lounge in Althouse Hall for a central but often quieter alternative to the library, located right on the historic academic quad.
cards.short_summary: A student lounge located within the historic Althouse Hall on the main academic quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Students identify the lounge in Althouse Hall as a favorite campus space for its location and atmosphere.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during standard academic building hours.

cards.title: Stern Great Room
cards.subtitle: Global education hub lounge
cards.notes: Relax in the Stern Great Room, a central space for the global education community that often hosts coffee hours and international events.
cards.short_summary: A large, multi-purpose room in the Stern Center used for both events and student relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stern Center includes the Stern Great Room, which is listed as a key location for campus events and student engagement.
cards.access_notes: Open during business hours; often used for scheduled global programming.

cards.title: Allison Hall Lounge
cards.subtitle: Expanded social and study space
cards.notes: Head to Allison Hall to find recently furnished lounge spaces that provide a more relaxed alternative to the formal Great Hall.
cards.short_summary: A furnished lounge area in Allison Hall designed to expand student social and study options.
cards.evidence_claim: Allison Hall was furnished to expand lounge space for students, providing more areas for activities and informal gathering.
cards.source_title: Allison Hall Furnished to Expand Lounge Space - The Dickinsonian
cards.access_notes: Available during building hours; check the online calendar for Great Hall events.

cards.title: Art & Art History Study Hallway
cards.subtitle: Creative corridor for art students
cards.notes: Walk through the Goodyear Building's study hallway, where art majors often gather near individual studio spaces and the student-run gallery.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated study and social corridor within the Goodyear Building art complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The Art and Art History Department facilities include an 'Art & Art History Study Hallway' in the Goodyear building alongside studio spaces.
cards.access_notes: Art majors have 24/7 key access; general gallery access is Tuesday-Saturday afternoons.

cards.title: Kaufman Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Sustainability and earth science hub
cards.notes: Study in the Kaufman Hall Reading Room (Room 118), a quiet spot located near the Center for Sustainability Education and the Museum of Earth Sciences.
cards.short_summary: A quiet reading room located on the first floor of Kaufman Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Kaufman Hall features a dedicated Reading Room (Room 118) on its first floor plan near the Geophysics and Microscopy labs.

cards.title: The Biblio Café
cards.subtitle: Library social study spot
cards.notes: Grab a coffee and find a seat in the Biblio Café; it's the designated 'loud' study area where talking is encouraged compared to the quiet upper floors.
cards.short_summary: A social study area and café located on the main floor of the library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Biblio Café is highlighted as a favorite student spot for relaxing and having coffee within the Waidner-Spahr Library.
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; café service hours may vary.
